To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oral bovine immunoglobin (Bovril) from hyperimmunised cows has previously been effective as prophylactic against E coli-induced diarrhoe and therapeutically for rotavirus and cryptospordia induced diarrhoea.

oral administration of a bovine immunoglobulins milk concentrate (BIMC) derived from immunized cows to children with ETEC/EPEC-induced diarrhoea did not reduce the severity or duration of the diarrhoea.
the BIC did not have any therapeutic benefit in treating EPEC/ETE-induced diarrhoea, and that it was well tolerated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of vaccines against diarrhoea.
the development of a new generation of oral immunotherapeutic agents to combat diarrhoea and other infectious diseases of childhood in the developing world.
the development and evaluation of oral bovine immunoglobin concentrate as a treatment for diarrhoea caused by ETEC and other diarrhoeagenie E.coli in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BIC is ineffective for treatment of diarrhoea caused by EPEC and ETEC.
Bovine Immune Milk is a very good prophylactic against ETEC and rotavirus, and a good therapeutic for Cryptosporidium, but it is not effective in treatment of acute EPEC/ETECDiarrhoea.
the BIC from immunized cows is not a therapeutic agent against E. coli induced diarrhoea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bovine Immunoglobin Milk Concentrate (BIMC) is effective in the prophylaxis of rotavirus-induced diarrhoea in children.
BIC has no therapeutic efficacy in E. coli induced diarrhoea.
the anti-E. coli antibodies were not effective in treating the children with ETEC/EPEC-induced diarrhoea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-E. coli antibodies in BIC were not able to prevent E. coli-induced diarrhea in children.
the anti-ETEC and anti-EPEC antibodies in BIC are not therapeutically efficacious in children with acute diarrhoea caused by ETEC and/or EPEC.

BIC from immunized cows can be used therapeutically in children with rotavirus and cryptospordiosis induced diarrhea, and that BIC from E. coli immunized cows is ineffective in the treatment of ETEC and/or EPEC-induced diarrhea.
